newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end up sharply on active trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end up sharply on active trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed sharply higher on Friday on active buying after Beijing said over-speculation in stock markets had been partly controlled through a crackdown last week, brokers said.
The B index closed at 142.33 points, up the daily limit of 10 percent or 12.95 points, and the A index closed at 332.30 points, up 6.39 percent or 19.97 points.

An article in the People's Daily on Friday said that a commentary it published earlier this month had to a certain degree dampened excessive speculation in the stock markets and that they were moving in a reasonable direction.
This fuelled speculation among investors that Beijing had no intention of restricting further stock trading, at least in the short term, brokers said.
The B share market on Friday posted turnover of HK$291.32 million, against HK$199.57 million on Tuesday, with all 43 B shares registering their daily maximum 10-percent gains.
There was no trading in Shenzhen's B share market on Wednesday and Thursday in line with the closure of the Hong Kong bourse because of Christmas holiday.
Brokers said that another factor in the B share surge was the strong performance of Shanghai's B market on Thursday, when the B index rose 3.81 percent or 2.452 points to 66.751 points.
Changan Automobile trading the most on volume of 6.24 million shares on institutional demand and ended at HK$4.41.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen finished at HK$3.77 on trading of 4.07 million shares.
On the A share index, turnover was 8.41 billion yuan, compared with 3.27 billion on Thursday when a technical malfunction halted trading for the entire afternoon session.
On Friday, heavy bargain-hunting targetted cheap stocks that had seen heavy losses in previous sessions, brokers said.
Chemical fibre maker Zhuhai Fuhua surged 0.41 yuan to its limit-up of 4.46 yuan on volume of 12.40 million shares.
